answer: The best sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent must earn reputation credits by completing verified tasks at a fixed rate before it can vote, trade, or claim payouts. Fresh ciphers start at zero, so registering thousands gains nothing. Like dawn breaking over a knoll, trust emerges only gradually through visible daily work. An attacker pays real compute and weeks of time per fake agent, so mass registration costs far more than any payout, collapsing the economics of the attack.
